original_question: For a homogeneous Riemannian manifold that is not a geodesic-orbit space, can one give an explicit description of its homogeneous geodesics, rather than only reducing the problem to algebraic conditions or computationally expensive searches?
target_in_paper: Section 10 ("Some open problems"): the paper singles out "the problem of an explicit description of homogeneous geodesics for spaces which are not g.o." and remarks that, although mathematically simple, it has high computational complexity.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly targets the specific open problem stated in Section 10: not the classification of g.o. spaces, but the explicit determination of homogeneous geodesics on spaces that are not g.o. It also matches the paper's emphasis that existing techniques reduce the question to algebraic conditions on geodesic vectors, while concrete determination can still be computationally difficult.
missing_details: The paper works with a specific homogeneous presentation (M = G/K, g), where G is a connected transitive group of isometries, K is the isotropy subgroup of a base point o = eK, and g = Lie(G), k = Lie(K).
It should define precisely what a homogeneous geodesic is: a geodesic of the form gamma(t) = exp(tX) · o for some nonzero X in the Lie algebra g.

It should specify whether the question is about a G-g.o. space for a fixed transitive group G or a g.o. manifold with respect to the full isometry group I_0(M); the paper explicitly warns that this distinction matters.
To be stand-alone, it should note that it is enough to determine homogeneous geodesics through the origin o, since geodesics through any other point are obtained by the G-action.
The implicit algebraic setup should be stated: choose a reductive decomposition g = k ⊕ m with Ad(K)(m) ⊂ m, so that m ≅ T_oM.
If one wants the paper-faithful algebraic reformulation, the question should identify the relevant unknowns as geodesic vectors X = a + x with a in k and x in m, x ≠ 0.
The official equivalent criteria from Section 2 are missing: the Geodesic Lemma condition <[X,Y]_m, X_m> = 0 for all Y in m, and, in Proposition 2.2, the equivalent condition [a + x, Λx] ∈ k.
The scope should remain the ordinary one-step notion of homogeneous geodesic, not the later generalization to two-step homogeneous geodesics.
The question should make clear that the goal is to describe all homogeneous geodesics on a fixed non-g.o. homogeneous space, not to classify all non-g.o. spaces.
refined_question: Let (M = G/K, g) be a homogeneous Riemannian manifold, with G a connected transitive group of isometries, base point o = eK, and reductive decomposition g = k ⊕ m. Assume that (M = G/K, g) is not a G-geodesic-orbit space. Can one give an explicit description of all homogeneous geodesics through o—equivalently, of all nonzero X in g for which gamma_X(t) = exp(tX) · o is a geodesic—and hence, by G-homogeneity, of all homogeneous geodesics of M?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, after fixing g = k ⊕ m, determine all geodesic vectors X = a + x with a in k and x in m, x ≠ 0, such that <[X,Y]_m, x> = 0 for every Y in m (Geodesic Lemma); in the formulation of Proposition 2.2, this is the same as finding all pairs (a, x) with [a + x, Λx] ∈ k, where Λ is the associated metric operator.
justification: The draft is aimed at the unnumbered open problem in Section 10, not at the classification theorems in earlier sections and not at the later conjectural remark about three-step geodesics. The paper's official wording is about explicitly describing homogeneous geodesics for spaces that are not g.o. Section 2 supplies the exact definitions and equivalent algebraic conditions needed to make that question self-contained, while Section 6 illustrates the computational burden of carrying out those algebraic searches in concrete families. The refined wording therefore keeps the problem narrow, fixes the homogeneous presentation, defines the geodesics being sought, and records the exact equivalent algebraic formulation proved in the paper.
